institution: Kaiser Permanente School of Allied Health Sciences
units: 90 quarter credits (quarter system, 8 quarters). Catalog: "the BBS requires specific curriculum, practicum hours, and credit minimums (90 quarter credits)"; the Academic Requirements table totals "Total Credits in Master of Science Degree 90.0". Credit load runs 14/14/14/14 in year one and 10/9/9/6 in year two.
length: 24 months, eight consecutive quarters, full time. Catalog: "The counseling program requires 24 months of study completed during eight academic quarters." One cohort start per year, in July. No part-time or extended track is published anywhere in the catalog or on the site.
format: Hybrid. The catalog files the degree as "(Distance Education)" and states: "Courses are offered in either distance education or in-person delivery with slightly more than half of coursework being delivered via distance education." Classes meet two afternoons/evenings a week - one in-person day and one online day (year one roughly 1:00-7:30pm in person, 2:00-7:30pm online; year two shorter). Catalog: "Synchronous online and in-person instruction occurs in the afternoon and/or evenings, while clinical experience is typically scheduled during normal business hours." In-person coursework is at the Richmond main campus, the San Mateo satellite (177 Bovet Rd), and, for students starting July 2026, the Lathrop satellite (17000 S. Harlan Rd). Three cohorts, one per campus, began July 2026; the curriculum is the same at all three.
city: Richmond, CA (main campus, 938 Marina Way South); satellite instructional sites in San Mateo and Lathrop, CA
tyear: 2026 (applies to the cohort starting Summer Quarter 2026, 7/6/2026; the tuition page states "Total costs and schedule of charges are valid as of 1/1/2026")

practicum.evidence: 2026 Academic Catalog, Clinical Assignments (p. 114): "Clinical assignments for all programs are made by the clinical coordinator in collaboration with the program director. Students may be required to travel long distances to receive full clinical education." || Counseling FAQs, answering "Will I be placed in a clinical site close to where I live?": "We are working with the Kaiser Permanente Northern California Mental Health Training Program to develop training sites. Our training locations are currently limited geographically, and we are working to expand across the region." || Program info-session deck: "Direct practice experiences are embedded in our training program in collaboration with the Kaiser Permanente Northern California Mental Health Training program" and "Clinical training will be hybrid with at least half of your time in-person at one of the Training Clinics across Northern California." || On post-graduate placement the deck is explicit that it is NOT guaranteed: "This is typically a full-time post-degree training experience under supervision of licensed mental providers. Students must apply for these competitive positions and placement is not guaranteed."
practicum.hours_direct: Catalog: "Students must also complete a minimum of 600 hours of supervised clinical experience to graduate. Of those hours, 225 must be direct patient care." Weekly load per the program's Clinical Training Timeline (reproduced in the info-session deck): quarters 3-4, "8 hours per week engaged in training experiences with the KP Mental Health Training Program" (observation; "These hours typically do not count toward licensure"); quarters 5-8, "16-24 hours per week engaged in direct clinical experiences under supervision of licensed mental health providers in the Mental Health Training Program", often 2-3 full days a week.

gre.evidence: No admission test appears anywhere in the catalog's Table 1.0 Application Requirements by Program for Counseling; the required items are online application, application fee, "Evidence of Prior Degrees (College Transcripts)", "Personal Statement", "Professional References and Recommendations" and "Resume". The one admission test the school uses is the Wonderlic, and the Admissions FAQ states: "Applicants for Medical Assisting and Phlebotomy are required to take and pass the Wonderlic." The catalog's own MSC admissions list is: "Hold a bachelor's degree (or higher) or its equivalent in any discipline", "Have earned a 3.0 Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA)", and the English proficiency requirement. The GRE is never mentioned in the 2026 catalog, the FAQs, or the apply-now page.
gre.min_gpa: 3.0 cumulative. Catalog: "The CGPA will be calculated based on the last 60 semester (or 90 quarter) units of the most recently completed bachelor's degree"; for applicants holding a graduate degree it is calculated on that degree alone. Below 3.0 is not an automatic bar: "Applicants with a CGPA below 3.0 will have an opportunity to provide additional information in their application essay." No subject prerequisites - FAQ: "Your prior degrees, either bachelor's or master's, can be in any discipline" - and no recency requirement. Additional required items: a 3-to-5-page double-spaced essay, a resume/CV, and two professional references. Application is through PsychologyCAS ($80 fee paid to PSYCAS).

other_accreditation: Institutional: WASC Senior College and University Commission (WSCUC), 1080 Marina Village Parkway, Suite 500, Alameda CA - "an institutional accrediting agency recognized by the United States Department of Education." Institutional approval to operate from the California Bureau for Private Postsecondary Education (BPPE). Programmatic: California Board of Behavioral Sciences approval for LMFT/AMFT licensure - the catalog cites "Business and Professions Code (BPC) section 498.36" (apparently a typo; the program page and FAQs cite section 4980.36, which is the correct LMFT degree-content statute).
note: Kaiser Permanente's own school runs a 90-quarter-credit, 24-month LMFT programme that takes roughly 20-25 students into a single July cohort each year and meets two afternoons or evenings a week - one day in person at Richmond, San Mateo or Lathrop, one day online. You do not go looking for a practicum: the school's clinical coordinator and program director make the clinical assignments, and training sits inside Kaiser Permanente's Northern California Mental Health Training Program, though the school says its training locations are "currently limited geographically" and that students "may be required to travel long distances". Tuition for the July 2026 cohort is $38,970 plus $1,265 in fees ($40,235 to the school, about $43,779 once books, screenings and licensure fees are added), and the school takes no federal aid at all - no FAFSA, no Title IV loans - so funding means a Kaiser private loan, employer help, or the Mental Health Scholars Academy scholarship of up to $19,485, which is "contingent upon completion of practicum at a Kaiser Permanente site". The programme has no COAMFTE accreditation; the school is WSCUC-accredited and the degree is BBS-approved for California licensure, and its published on-time completion rates are 85% for the 2023 intake and 79% for 2024.
still_unknown: part-time or extended-completion option - none is published; the catalog describes only a fixed full-time 24-month, eight-quarter cohort

application closing date for the next (July 2027) cohort - the program page publishes only "Applications will open September 2026"; the prior cycle's stated deadline was January 31, 2026 on the legacy program page

whether graduates are hired into Kaiser Permanente - no hiring rate or pipeline claim is published; the BPPE School Performance Fact Sheet reports a 0% in-field job placement rate for the 2023 and 2024 cohorts, which reflects BPPE's employment definition applied to graduates who are still accruing AMFT hours, not a measured hiring outcome

explicit per-credit tuition rate - the catalog publishes only per-quarter tuition; $433/quarter credit is arithmetic ($38,970 total tuition / 90 credits, and $6,062 / 14 credits), consistent across every quarter in the 2026 Schedule of Student Charges
the program's Clinical Training Timeline PDF is image-only with no extractable text; its content was read from the info-session slide deck, which reproduces it verbatim
